My issue wise findings in the case are as under :-
1. Whether on 06.07.2017 at about 8:40 pm, Sector7/8 Dividing Road in front of Nav Durga Mandir, Bus Stand, M2K to Sai Baba Chowk on road, Delhi was driving Scooter (LML) bearing registration no. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim MACT Case No.759/17 (FIR no. 301/17) Anita Vs.

sentences.text: The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.

The non- pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed which includes the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
23.

24. In light of the above legal prepositions, the amount of compensation which could be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this tribunal shall be as under:-
Medical or Treatment Expenses:
25.
Petitioner has placed on judicial filed her medical bills Ex.PW-1/E to Ex.PW-1/O for an amount of Rs.80,373/-.

Apart from this, the petitioner has filed the estimate expenditure of transplant surgery of iron rod in the left leg issued from Hasija Hospital, Trauma Care Centre for an amount of Rs.80,000/- - Rs. 1,00,000/-.
Keeping in view of this, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.80,373/-+ Rs.1,00,000/- = Rs.1,80,373/- under this head.
Pain and Suffering 26.
As per the MLC, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the above accident.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which she actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate her for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner, disability of petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs. 50,000/- is being awarded to her towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
Thus, she is awarded a total amount of Rs. 50,000/- under this head.

The petitioner has deposed in her evidence affidavit that at the relevant time, she was doing stitching and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In order to support her abovesaid claim as to her employment and monthly income, petitioner has not filed any documents on record.
Petitioner had filed Ex.PW-1/C i.e. copy of degree of MA.
In the above facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to Graduate person in Delhi at the relevant time.
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to Graduate person as on 06.07.2017 in the Delhi were Rs.17,916/- per month.

Keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner as well as her prolonged medical treatment,
it could be safely assumed that the petitioner would not have been able to resume her work/
vocation for 2 months.
As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.35,832/- (Rs.17,916/- x 2).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
Conveyance, Attendant and Special Diet 28.
Petitioner has claimed a sum for special diet, for conveyance and for attendant charges.
However, she failed to place on record any corroborative material in this regard.
In view of the nature of injuries sustained by him, a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner cumulatively under these heads.

that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.
The copies of FIR, Chargesheet and MLC, also corroborate the oral testimony of PW1.
In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is of considered opinion that R-1 is guilty of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle at the relevant time leading to the accident in which petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
20. The medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner shows that he suffered grievous injuries on account of neglect and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
22. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MACT Case No.759/17 (FIR no. 301/17)
Anita Vs. Abhilesh Sharma & Ors.
 Page no. 8 of 14
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as Anita vs Abhilesh Sharma And Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180740586/
6 non- pecuniary damages.
The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.
The non- pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed which includes the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner, disability of petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs. 50,000/- is being awarded to her towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
In the above facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate that the monthly income of petitioner be assessed as per the minimum wages payable to Graduate person in Delhi at the relevant time.
